- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecasts tend to be too high in the first 5–10 days of the 30-day window, then gradually adjust — suggesting a lag in recognizing short-term mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., 75+), model often overshoots in the immediate aftermath, then underestimates the subsequent decline.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values when recent history includes high prices (e.g., 75+), failing to reflect mean reversion toward lower levels.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days of the forecast horizon, especially when true outcomes show rapid downward correction.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of downward corrections after spikes, particularly in the 10–20 day range.
- When true prices dip below 70, model often fails to recognize the trend and continues to forecast higher values.
- Model shows strong tendency to “smooth” volatility — underestimating sharp drops and overestimating gradual declines.
- Forecasts are more accurate when the 30-day history includes a recent low (e.g., 68–70), suggesting model adjusts better to bottoming trends.
- Model tends to overcorrect after a low, forecasting a rebound too aggressively — especially in the 10–15 day window.
